Ownership and succession

Succession-led acquisitions

An owner hands the business to a successor who can carry its people, knowledge and customer relationships forward.

Who it suits
Founders and families weighing who should lead next.
Typical objectives
Protect continuity, agree the founder’s future role and plan the handover.
Our role
We discuss what the family wants to preserve, identify potential successors and plan introductions around the owner’s preferences.
Discuss this transaction ↗

Ownership and succession

Full and majority business exits

A sale of the entire business or a controlling stake, with scope for the owner to retain an agreed interest.

Who it suits
Owners considering retirement, a change of role or a partial exit.
Typical objectives
Choose how much to sell, what involvement to retain and which buyer fits.
Our role
We compare ownership routes, agree an approach to buyers and coordinate diligence with the owner’s advisers.
Discuss this transaction ↗

Ownership and succession

Family-to-family acquisitions

One business family acquires an enterprise from another, often with a shared interest in long-term ownership.

Who it suits
Business families seeking a successor or an adjacent business to own.
Typical objectives
Find alignment on culture, stewardship and the outgoing family’s involvement.
Our role
We discuss both families’ priorities and bring them together when expectations on control and continuity align.
Discuss this transaction ↗

Ownership and succession

Business continuity planning

Preparation for a transfer of ownership while the business keeps serving customers and supporting its team.

Who it suits
Owners whose relationships or operating decisions still depend heavily on them.
Typical objectives
Identify key dependencies and agree which responsibilities transfer first.
Our role
We work through the handover with the owners and incoming team, alongside their professional advisers.
Discuss this transaction ↗

Ownership and succession

Management-led ownership transitions

An existing management team explores taking ownership of the business it already runs.

Who it suits
Experienced managers and owners who want continuity in day-to-day leadership.
Typical objectives
Keep operating knowledge in place and clarify future ownership and governance.
Our role
We help the parties define their objectives, explore suitable funding relationships and coordinate the transaction process.
Discuss this transaction ↗

Ownership and succession

Entrepreneurship through acquisition

An entrepreneur buys and runs an established company, building on its existing team, customers and operations.

Who it suits
Operators, industry specialists and searchers who want to become business owners.
Typical objectives
Find a business that fits the operator’s skills and the founder’s succession priorities.
Our role
We help define a search, identify relevant businesses and introduce aligned owners or capital partners where appropriate.
Discuss this transaction ↗

Corporate growth and strategic acquisitions

Business-to-business acquisitions

An established company buys another operating business to add a product, capability or customer base.

Who it suits
Promoter-led groups and companies pursuing an acquisition within or alongside their existing operations.
Typical objectives
Bring complementary activities under shared ownership and assess how the businesses could work together.
Our role
We translate the buyer’s requirements into a target profile, qualify potential sellers and coordinate introductions.
Discuss this transaction ↗

Corporate growth and strategic acquisitions

Strategic buyouts

A corporate buyer takes control of a business that advances a specific growth priority.

Who it suits
Corporate development teams and strategic buyers with a defined capability gap.
Typical objectives
Add capacity, enter a product line or secure a critical part of the supply chain.
Our role
We map potential targets to the buyer’s priorities and help both sides evaluate the fit before diligence.
Discuss this transaction ↗

Corporate growth and strategic acquisitions

Roll-ups and consolidation

A buyer acquires several complementary businesses around a shared operating platform.

Who it suits
Acquisition teams building a group in a fragmented industry.
Typical objectives
Build scale across locations or specialties while assessing how each acquisition can be integrated.
Our role
We define the acquisition criteria, identify potential anchor and add-on businesses, and coordinate discussions with owners.
Discuss this transaction ↗

Corporate growth and strategic acquisitions

Sector consolidation

A business combines with peers in the same industry to deepen its market coverage.

Who it suits
Established sector participants seeking greater density or a broader customer mix.
Typical objectives
Evaluate overlapping capacity, complementary accounts and integration priorities.
Our role
We map the sector, screen businesses against the mandate and facilitate discussions with interested owners.
Discuss this transaction ↗

Corporate growth and strategic acquisitions

Geographic expansion

A buyer enters a new region through an established local business.

Who it suits
Companies seeking regional distribution, operating capacity or customer access.
Typical objectives
Understand the value of local relationships, routes to market and regional management.
Our role
We source within the target geography and qualify local businesses against the buyer’s expansion brief.
Discuss this transaction ↗

Corporate growth and strategic acquisitions

Corporate deal scouting

A focused search for potential acquisitions against a company’s own buying criteria.

Who it suits
Corporate development teams with a defined mandate and limited local coverage.
Typical objectives
Find relevant off-market businesses and understand owner interest before committing resources.
Our role
We agree a search brief, use our origination network to identify prospects and bring forward qualified introductions.
Discuss this transaction ↗

Capital-led acquisitions

Private equity buyouts

A private equity investor acquires a controlling interest in an established company.

Who it suits
Buyout investors with a defined mandate and owners open to institutional ownership.
Typical objectives
Align sector, size, control requirements and plans for the business.
Our role
We source against the investment mandate and coordinate introductions and transaction discussions.
Discuss this transaction ↗

Capital-led acquisitions

Micro private equity

An acquisition investor focuses on smaller established businesses, often with hands-on ownership.

Who it suits
Specialist buyout firms and acquisition investors with a clear operating thesis.
Typical objectives
Find businesses where the investor’s sector knowledge or operating partners could contribute.
Our role
We screen for ownership fit, understand founder priorities and identify relevant operating relationships.
Discuss this transaction ↗

Capital-led acquisitions

Family office-led acquisitions

A family office acquires a direct ownership stake in an operating business.

Who it suits
Family offices and investment holding companies seeking direct business ownership.
Typical objectives
Match sector knowledge, preferred control and intended holding horizon.
Our role
We work from the family’s mandate and introduce owners whose objectives fit its approach.
Discuss this transaction ↗

Capital-led acquisitions

Investor-backed ownership transitions

An investor supports a change of ownership with an incoming operator or an existing management team.

Who it suits
Investors, operators and founders exploring a shared transition.
Typical objectives
Align financial participation, management responsibility and decision-making before an acquisition.
Our role
We identify relevant counterparties and help the parties clarify roles before detailed evaluation.
Discuss this transaction ↗

Capital-led acquisitions

Search fund-backed acquisitions

A search entrepreneur pursues an established business with the support of acquisition investors.

Who it suits
Search fund teams and investors who back entrepreneurs to own and operate companies.
Typical objectives
Find an owner willing to transition and a business suited to the incoming leader.
Our role
We help refine search criteria, surface relevant businesses and coordinate discussions among owners, searchers and investors.
Discuss this transaction ↗

Cross-border acquisitions

Foreign buyouts

An overseas buyer acquires an Indian business, subject to applicable legal, tax and regulatory requirements.

Who it suits
International strategic buyers, investment firms and business families evaluating Indian ownership opportunities.
Typical objectives
Assess local fit and align ownership, diligence and transition expectations.
Our role
We originate Indian businesses against the buyer’s brief and coordinate discussions alongside qualified advisers.

Cross-border transactions are subject to applicable legal, tax and regulatory requirements.

Discuss this transaction ↗

Cross-border acquisitions

International strategic acquisitions

A corporate acquirer seeks an Indian business that complements its global operations.

Who it suits
International manufacturers and service businesses with a specific capability requirement.
Typical objectives
Evaluate manufacturing depth, talent, suppliers or complementary product lines in India.
Our role
We assess the industrial fit, establish owner interest and support coordination across the two teams.

Cross-border transactions are subject to applicable legal, tax and regulatory requirements.

Discuss this transaction ↗

Cross-border acquisitions

India market entry through acquisition

An international buyer establishes a local presence by acquiring an existing Indian operation.

Who it suits
Businesses comparing acquisition with building a local operation from the ground up.
Typical objectives
Assess customers, operating capacity and leadership already in place.
Our role
We define the India entry brief and identify businesses whose footprint fits the buyer’s plans.

Cross-border transactions are subject to applicable legal, tax and regulatory requirements.

Discuss this transaction ↗

Cross-border acquisitions

Cross-border sourcing relationships

An overseas acquisition team works with a local origination partner to identify potential businesses in India.

Who it suits
International acquisition teams seeking local access and context.
Typical objectives
Build a relevant target list and establish whether owners are open to a conversation.
Our role
We connect the search brief with our pan-India origination network and qualify opportunities before introductions.

Illustrative coverage

Inside the sectors.

A look at what shapes an acquisition conversation in each industry. Availability depends on the mandate.

Manufacturing and industrials

Plant capability, capacity, customer relationships and the operating team that keeps production moving.

Chemicals and specialty materials

Product mix, process knowledge, customer qualifications and the facilities needed to meet them.

Healthcare and pharmaceuticals

Service footprint, manufacturing capability, quality systems and continuity of operations.

Education

Institutional continuity, leadership, facilities and relationships with students and families.

Automotive and engineering

Component capability, customer programmes, tooling and the depth of engineering talent.

Consumer businesses

Brand strength, distribution reach, repeat demand and the economics of individual channels.

Logistics and distribution

Route density, customer contracts, fleet requirements and the reach of the distribution network.

Technology and business services

Client relationships, recurring work, specialist talent and the delivery model behind the business.

Hospitality and commercial assets

Property operations, operator agreements, location economics and the intended ownership structure.

Our process

From the first conversation
to the next chapter.

01 / Understand

Start with the people involved. We listen to the owner’s priorities and the acquirer’s requirements, including what each wants to preserve.

02 / Structure

Define the preferred stake, timing, strategic fit and terms that will guide the search.

03 / Originate

Identify suitable businesses or counterparties, qualify the fit and agree what can be shared.

04 / Execute

Coordinate introductions, negotiations and diligence alongside the parties and their professional advisers.

05 / Transition

Support the handover of relationships, responsibilities and operating knowledge to the next owner.
